Bitcoin ETFs Draw $110 Million as Ether Funds Shed $88.6 Million

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $110 million in net inflows on October 26, entirely driven by BlackRock's IBIT, bringing its cumulative net inflows to $66.24 billion. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $88.58 million in net outflows, although Fidelity's FETH led individual fund inflows with $16.13 million. BlackRock is the world's largest asset manager, while Fidelity is one of the largest U.S. investment firms. — link

Hyperliquid announced that Kraken parent Payward plans to become the first CFTC-regulated HIP-3* deployer, using Hyperliquid infrastructure to offer perpetual futures markets to U.S. clients. Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Hoodi Fork Over EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 Risks

Ethereum researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the planned Glamsterdam fork on the Hoodi testnet has been delayed after ChainSecurity identified compatibility risks in EIP-8037 and EIP-8038. The gas changes could break contracts that assume gas usage only decreases or cause failed sub-calls to behave unexpectedly. ChainSecurity has found 13 real-world cases, and developers are reviewing whether the upgrade specification needs changes. — link
